You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
The Lamb

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES

{
  "primary_meaning": "In Christian teaching, 'the Lamb' overwhelmingly refers to Jesus Christ as the sacrificial, atoning offering for sin — the 'Lamb of God' whose death takes away the sins of the world. The image fuses the Passover lamb of the Exodus, the lambs of the Levitical sacrificial system, and the suffering servant 'led like a lamb to the slaughter,' and it culminates in the exalted 'Lamb who was slain' worshiped in Revelation. Innocence, purity (being 'without blemish'), voluntary submission to death, redemptive substitution, and — in Revelation — paradoxical victory and kingship through sacrifice are the standard associated ideas.",

  "notes": "This is one of the most stable and widely attested symbols in Christian interpretation, affirmed across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions (e.g., the liturgical 'Agnus Dei') and across academic biblical scholarship. Disagreements concern which Old Testament background is primary (Passover lamb, Isaiah 53 servant, Tamid, Akedah) and how much Revelation's Lamb subverts versus embodies militant messianism — not whether the Lamb symbolizes Christ and his redemptive death. The secondary use of lamb imagery for believers is universally recognized but treated as distinct from the christological title."

BOOK ENTRY
Jesus Christ — the unblemished Passover sacrifice, slain to redeem His people and now reigning.

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
(none)

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Ex 12:5; Isa 53:7; John 1:29; 1 Cor 5:7; 1 Pet 1:18-19; Rev 5:6-13)

Revelation 5:7 — And he came and took the book out of the right hand of him that sat upon the throne.
Revelation 5:8 — And when he had taken the book, the four beasts and four and twenty elders fell down before the Lamb, having every one of them harps, and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints.
Revelation 5:9 — And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation;

Revelation 5:12 — Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.
Revelation 5:13 — And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever.

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
